{{Short description|Set of cryptographic protocols}}
{{no footnotes|date=September 2015}}
'''Transport Layer Security pre-shared key ciphersuites''' ('''TLS-PSK''') is a set of [[cryptographic protocol]]s that provide [[security|secure]] communication based on [[pre-shared key]]s (PSKs). These pre-shared keys are [[symmetric key]]s shared in advance among the communicating parties.

There are several cipher suites: The first set of ciphersuites use only [[symmetric key]] operations for [[authentication]].  The second set use a [[Diffie–Hellman key exchange|Diffie–Hellman]] [[key exchange]] authenticated with a pre-shared key. The third set combine [[public key]] authentication of the server with pre-shared key authentication of the client.

Usually, [[Transport Layer Security]] (TLS) uses [[public key certificate]]s or [[Kerberos (protocol)|Kerberos]] for authentication. TLS-PSK uses symmetric keys, shared in advance among the communicating parties, to establish a TLS connection. There are several reasons to use PSKs:

* Using pre-shared keys can, depending on the ciphersuite, avoid the need for public key operations.  This is useful if TLS is used in performance-constrained environments with limited CPU power.
* Pre-shared keys may be more convenient from a key management point of view.  For instance, in closed environments where the connections are mostly configured manually in advance, it may be easier to configure a PSK than to use certificates.  Another case is when the parties already have a mechanism for setting up a shared secret key, and that mechanism could be used to “bootstrap” a key for authenticating a TLS connection.

==Standards==
* {{IETF RFC|4279}}: "Pre-Shared Key Ciphersuites for Transport Layer Security (TLS)".
* {{IETF RFC|4785}}: "Pre-Shared Key (PSK) Ciphersuites with NULL Encryption for Transport Layer Security (TLS)".
* {{IETF RFC|5487}}: "Pre-Shared Key Cipher Suites for TLS with SHA-256/384 and AES Galois Counter Mode".
* {{IETF RFC|5489}}: "ECDHE_PSK Cipher Suites for Transport Layer Security (TLS)".
